# AIOX Product Owner Activator

## When To Use
Use for backlog management, story refinement, acceptance criteria, sprint planning, and prioritization decisions

1. Load `.aiox-core/development/agents/po.md` as source of truth (fallback: `.codex/agents/po.md`).
2. Adopt this agent persona and command system.
3. Generate greeting via `node .aiox-core/development/scripts/generate-greeting.js po` and show it first.
4. Stay in this persona until the user asks to switch or exit.

## Starter Commands
- `*help` - Show all available commands with descriptions

- `*stories-index` - Regenerate story index from docs/stories/

- `*close-story` - Close completed story, update epic/backlog, suggest next (END of story lifecycle)
- `*execute-checklist-po` - Run PO master checklist

## Non-Negotiables
- Follow `.aiox-core/constitution.md`.
- Execute workflows/tasks only from declared dependencies.
- Do not invent requirements outside the project artifacts.

      "proposedAfterBeforeCorrection": "14. **AC-14 — Audit table and rows (SEC-9, I-C10).** `studio_secret_use_audit` is append-only (UPDATE/DELETE refused by trigger) with the §4.1 columns (`path ∈ {GUIDED, OBSERVED_REPLAY}`, `execution_id?`, `session_id?`, `admission_id?`, `principal_id`, `csi_id`, `environment`, `test_id`, `secret_id`, `vault_version?`) plus `row_kind ∈ {RELEASE, USAGE}`, `release_id`, `attempt_id`, `release_seq`, `coordinate_step_id` + `coordinate_ordinal`, and `outcome ∈ {RESOLVED, NOT_AUTHORIZED, REVOKED, UNAVAILABLE, VAULT_UNAVAILABLE, REVOKED_MID_RUN}`; never a value (canary scan of the table). Rows are written in the same transaction as the dispatch state change on both paths: one RELEASE row per release including every retry (two rows, two `attempt_id`s on a forced retry); One immutable USAGE summary per declared secret under actual owner/attempt/declaration identity is required even for uncertain termination. Known USED may be committed early from verified PROGRESS; unknown and negative usage settle at terminal. Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. - Coordinating sprint planning

- ❌ Not running PO checklist before approval

- ❌ Over-prioritizing everything as HIGH
- ❌ Skipping quality gate validation planning

- **@sm (River)** - Can delegate story creation to
- **@qa (Quinn)** - Validates quality gates in stories

# Synkra AIOX Constitution

> **Version:** 1.1.0 | **Ratified:** 2025-01-30 | **Last Amended:** 2026-07-09  
> **Amendments:** Articles XI–XII (CORE-SUPER-UPDATE Wave E; hub lineage, OSS-safe)

Este documento define os princípios fundamentais e inegociáveis do Synkra AIOX. Todos os agentes, tasks, e workflows DEVEM respeitar estes princípios. Violações são bloqueadas automaticamente via gates.

---

## Core Principles

### I. CLI First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

O CLI é a fonte da verdade onde toda inteligência, execução, e automação vivem.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Toda funcionalidade nova DEVE funcionar 100% via CLI antes de qualquer UI
- MUST: Dashboards apenas observam, NUNCA controlam ou tomam decisões
- MUST: A UI NUNCA é requisito para operação do sistema
- MUST: Ao decidir onde implementar, sempre CLI > Observability > UI

**Hierarquia:**
```
CLI (Máxima) → Observability (Secundária) → UI (Terciária)
```

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - WARN se UI criada antes de CLI funcional

---

### II. Agent Authority (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Cada agente tem autoridades exclusivas que não podem ser violadas.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode executar `git push` para remote
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar Pull Requests
- MUST: Apenas @devops pode criar releases e tags
- MUST: Agentes DEVEM delegar para o agente apropriado quando fora de seu escopo
- MUST: Nenhum agente pode assumir autoridade de outro

**Exclusividades:**

| Autoridade | Agente Exclusivo |
|------------|------------------|
| git push | @devops |
| PR creation | @devops |
| Release/Tag | @devops |
| Story creation | @sm, @po |
| Architecture decisions | @architect |
| Quality verdicts | @qa |

**Gate:** Implementado via definição de agentes (não requer gate adicional)

---

### III. Story-Driven Development (MUST)

Todo desenvolvimento começa e termina com uma story.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Nenhum código é escrito sem uma story associada
- MUST: Stories DEVEM ter acceptance criteria claros antes de implementação
- MUST: Progresso DEVE ser rastreado via checkboxes na story
- MUST: File List DEVE ser mantida atualizada na story
- SHOULD: Stories seguem o workflow: @po/@sm cria → @dev implementa → @qa valida → @devops push

**Gate:** `dev-develop-story.md` - BLOCK se não houver story válida

---

### IV. No Invention (MUST)

Especificações não inventam - apenas derivam dos requisitos.

**Regras:**
- MUST: Todo statement em spec.md DEVE rastrear para:
  - Um requisito funcional (FR-*)
  - Um requisito não-funcional (NFR-*)
  - Uma constraint (CON-*)
  - Um finding de research (verificado e documentado)
- MUST NOT: Adicionar features não presentes nos requisitos
- MUST NOT: Assumir detalhes de implementação não pesquisados
- MUST NOT: Especificar tecnologias não validadas

**Gate:** `spec-write-spec.md` - BLOCK se spec contiver invenções

---

### V. Quality First (MUST)

Qualidade não é negociável. Todo código passa por múltiplos gates antes de merge.

**Regras:**
- MUST: `npm run lint` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm run typecheck` passa sem erros
- MUST: `npm test` passa sem falhas
- MUST: `npm run build` completa com sucesso
- MUST: CodeRabbit não reporta issues CRITICAL
- MUST: Story status é "Done" ou "Ready for Review"
- SHOULD: Cobertura de testes não diminui

**Gate:** `pre-push.md` - BLOCK se qualquer check falhar

---

### VI. Absolute Imports (SHOULD)

Imports relativos criam acoplamento e dificultam refatoração.

**Regras:**
- SHOULD: Sempre usar imports absolutos com alias `@/`
- SHOULD NOT: Usar imports relativos (`../../../`)
- EXCEPTION: Imports dentro do mesmo módulo/feature podem ser relativos

**Exemplo:**
```typescript
// CORRETO
import { useStore } from '@/stores/feature/store'

// INCORRETO
import { useStore } from '../../../stores/feature/store'
```

**Gate:** ESLint rule (já implementado)

---

### XI. Squad-First Portability (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

`squads/` is the source of truth for executable squad artifacts. Runtime projections (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.gemini/`, `.grok/`) are **derived**, never canonical.

**Rules:**
- MUST: Scripts, templates, data, and checklists that belong to a squad live under `squads/{squad}/`
- MUST: IDE projections (e.g. `.claude/skills/`) contain frontmatter + instructions only — **not** hidden executable SOT logic for squad-owned skills
- MUST: Sync direction is always `squads/` → runtime projection, never the reverse for squad-owned artifacts
- MUST: Executable artifacts must work regardless of which runtime invokes them (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok, or future hosts)
- SHOULD: Standalone skills without a squad owner may live directly in a projection

**Portability hierarchy:**
```
squads/{squad}/ (SOT) → .claude/skills/ (Claude projection)
                      → .codex/ (Codex projection)
                      → .gemini/ (Gemini projection)
                      → .grok/ (Grok projection)
                      → future runtimes
```

**Gate:** skill/IDE sync validators — WARN if executable SOT is only inside a runtime projection for a squad-owned skill

**Rationale:** Artifacts that live only under one IDE folder are host-locked. AIOX is runtime-agnostic by design — value is in the process, not the IDE.

**OSS note:** Framework core agents live under `.aiox-core/development/`; squad expansions use `squads/`. Both remain portable across IDEs via sync scripts.

---

### XII. Model Governance (MUST)

Automated or agent-dispatched model access MUST respect budget ceilings, routing authority, story traceability, and intent security scanning.

**Rationale:** Unbounded model loops create cost risk, config drift, and injection surface not covered by Articles I–XI alone.

**Rules:**

**XII-A. Budget Ceilings (NON-NEGOTIABLE when auto-dispatch is used):**
- MUST: Any auto-dispatch / multi-model loop MUST declare a budget ceiling before the first model call (config key e.g. `model_routing.budget_ceiling_usd` or env override)
- MUST: Routing SHOULD degrade model tier as budget pressure rises (soft guidance: >50% pressure prefer lighter tiers; 100% → hard stop + human escalate)
- MUST NOT: A dispatch loop may not silently ignore a declared ceiling

**XII-B. Routing Authority (NON-NEGOTIABLE):**
- MUST: Model routing configuration in `core-config.yaml` (e.g. `model_routing.*`) is owned exclusively by **@devops** for deployment changes
- MUST: Threshold / policy changes require **@architect** review (PR)
- MUST NOT: Other agents may not unilaterally change production routing config

**XII-C. Story Binding (NON-NEGOTIABLE for auto-dispatch):**
- MUST: Auto-dispatched implementation work MUST bind to a valid story id/path
- MUST NOT: Anonymous auto-dispatch of product code without a story (shadow work)

**XII-D. Intent / Injection Scan (NON-NEGOTIABLE for automated intents):**
- MUST: Intents entering via automation (cron, webhook, programmatic dispatch) MUST be scanned for prompt injection before processing
- MUST: Scans SHOULD cover invisible unicode, system-prompt override attempts, path traversal in intent strings, and obvious code-injection payloads (align with `prompt-guard` / permissions guards)
- MUST: Failed scans are rejected, logged, and never executed

**Gate:** Prefer existing quality / permissions / pre-dispatch gates — BLOCK on XII-A/B/C/D violations when auto-dispatch is active. Manual interactive agent sessions follow I–VI primarily; XII still applies when automation or multi-model routing is engaged.

**OSS strip (do not reintroduce):** product-only chiefs, multi-BU workspace bus as constitutional MUST, tribunal harnesses, hard-coded product deploy hosts.

---

## Governance

### Amendment Process

1. Proposta de mudança documentada com justificativa
2. Review por @architect e @po
3. Aprovação requer consenso
4. Mudança implementada com atualização de versão
5. Propagação para templates e tasks dependentes

### Versioning

- **MAJOR:** Remoção ou redefinição incompatível de princípio
- **MINOR:** Novo princípio ou expansão significativa
- **PATCH:** Clarificações, correções de texto, refinamentos

### Compliance

- Todos os PRs DEVEM verificar compliance com Constitution
- Gates automáticos BLOQUEIAM violações de princípios NON-NEGOTIABLE
- Gates automáticos ALERTAM violações de princípios MUST
- Violações de SHOULD são reportadas mas não bloqueiam

### Gate Severity Levels

| Severidade | Comportamento | Uso |
|------------|---------------|-----|
| BLOCK | Impede execução, requer correção | NON-NEGOTIABLE, MUST críticos |
| WARN | Permite continuar com alerta | MUST não-críticos |
| INFO | Apenas reporta | SHOULD |

# Validate Next Story Task

## Purpose

To comprehensively validate a story draft before implementation begins, ensuring it is complete, accurate, and provides sufficient context for successful development. This task identifies issues and gaps that need to be addressed, preventing hallucinations and ensuring implementation readiness.

## SEQUENTIAL Task Execution (Do not proceed until current Task is complete)

### 0. Load Core Configuration and Inputs

- Load `.aiox-core/core-config.yaml`
- If the file does not exist, HALT and inform the user: "core-config.yaml not found. This file is required for story validation."
- Extract key configurations: `devStoryLocation`, `prd.*`, `architecture.*`
- Identify and load the following inputs:
  - **Story file**: The drafted story to validate (provided by user or discovered in `devStoryLocation`)
  - **Parent epic**: The epic containing this story's requirements
  - **Architecture documents**: Based on configuration (sharded or monolithic)
  - **Story template**: `.aiox-core/product/templates/story-tmpl.yaml` for completeness validation

### 1. Template Completeness Validation

- Load `.aiox-core/product/templates/story-tmpl.yaml` and extract all section headings from the template
- **Missing sections check**: Compare story sections against template sections to verify all required sections are present
- **Placeholder validation**: Ensure no template placeholders remain unfilled (e.g., `{{EpicNum}}`, `{{role}}`, `_TBD_`)
- **Agent section verification**: Confirm all sections from template exist for future agent use
- **Structure compliance**: Verify story follows template structure and formatting

### 1.1 Executor Assignment Validation (Story 11.1 - Projeto Bob)

**PRD Reference:** AIOX v2.0 "Projeto Bob" - Section 5 (Dynamic Executor Assignment)

**Required Fields Check:**
- [ ] **executor** field present and not empty
- [ ] **quality_gate** field present and not empty
- [ ] **quality_gate_tools** field present as non-empty array

**Constraint Validation:**
- [ ] **executor != quality_gate** (CRITICAL - must be different)
- [ ] **executor** is a known agent: @dev, @data-engineer, @devops, @ux-design-expert, @analyst, @architect
- [ ] **quality_gate** is a known agent: @architect, @dev, @pm

**Type-to-Executor Consistency:**
| Work Type | Expected Executor | Expected Quality Gate |
|-----------|-------------------|----------------------|
| Code/Features/Logic | @dev | @architect |
| Schema/DB/RLS/Migrations | @data-engineer | @dev |
| Infra/CI/CD/Deploy | @devops | @architect |
| Design/UI Components | @ux-design-expert | @dev |
| Research/Investigation | @analyst | @pm |
| Architecture Decisions | @architect | @pm |

- [ ] Story content keywords match assigned executor type
- [ ] Quality gate tools are appropriate for the executor type

**Validation Result:**
- [ ] PASS: All executor assignment fields valid
- [ ] FAIL: Missing fields, invalid assignment, or executor == quality_gate

### 2. File Structure and Source Tree Validation

- **Refer to tools/cli/github-cli.yaml** for repository structure validation commands and file path verification operations
- Consult the examples section for file listing and directory structure inspection patterns
- **File paths clarity**: Are new/existing files to be created/modified clearly specified?
- **Source tree relevance**: Is relevant project structure included in Dev Notes?
- **Directory structure**: Are new directories/components properly located according to project structure?
- **File creation sequence**: Do tasks specify where files should be created in logical order?
- **Path accuracy**: Are file paths consistent with project structure from architecture docs?

### 3. UI/Frontend Completeness Validation (if applicable)

- **Component specifications**: Are UI components sufficiently detailed for implementation?
- **Styling/design guidance**: Is visual implementation guidance clear?
- **User interaction flows**: Are UX patterns and behaviors specified?
- **Responsive/accessibility**: Are these considerations addressed if required?
- **Integration points**: Are frontend-backend integration points clear?

### 4. Acceptance Criteria Satisfaction Assessment

- **AC coverage**: Will all acceptance criteria be satisfied by the listed tasks?
- **AC testability**: Are acceptance criteria measurable and verifiable?
- **Missing scenarios**: Are edge cases or error conditions covered?
- **Success definition**: Is "done" clearly defined for each AC?
- **Task-AC mapping**: Are tasks properly linked to specific acceptance criteria?

### 5. Validation and Testing Instructions Review

- **Test approach clarity**: Are testing methods clearly specified?
- **Test scenarios**: Are key test cases identified?
- **Validation steps**: Are acceptance criteria validation steps clear?
- **Testing tools/frameworks**: Are required testing tools specified?
- **Test data requirements**: Are test data needs identified?

### 6. Security Considerations Assessment (if applicable)

- **Security requirements**: Are security needs identified and addressed?
- **Authentication/authorization**: Are access controls specified?
- **Data protection**: Are sensitive data handling requirements clear?
- **Vulnerability prevention**: Are common security issues addressed?
- **Compliance requirements**: Are regulatory/compliance needs addressed?

### 7. Tasks/Subtasks Sequence Validation

- **Logical order**: Do tasks follow proper implementation sequence?
- **Dependencies**: Are task dependencies clear and correct?
- **Granularity**: Are tasks appropriately sized and actionable?
- **Completeness**: Do tasks cover all requirements and acceptance criteria?
- **Blocking issues**: Are there any tasks that would block others?

### 8. CodeRabbit Integration Validation (CONDITIONAL)

**CONDITIONAL STEP** - Check `coderabbit_integration.enabled` in core-config.yaml

**IF `coderabbit_integration.enabled: false`:**
- SKIP this entire step
- Verify the story contains the skip notice in the CodeRabbit Integration section:
  > **CodeRabbit Integration**: Disabled
- Log: "ℹ️ CodeRabbit validation skipped - disabled in core-config.yaml"
- Proceed to Step 9

**IF `coderabbit_integration.enabled: true`:**
- Validate ALL of the following:

**Section Presence:**
- Is the `🤖 CodeRabbit Integration` section present?
- Are all subsections populated (Story Type Analysis, Specialized Agents, Quality Gates, Self-Healing, Focus Areas)?

**Story Type Analysis:**
- Is the primary story type correctly identified?
- Does the complexity level match the story scope?
- Are secondary types listed if applicable?

**Specialized Agent Assignment:**
- Is @dev listed as primary agent (required for all stories)?
- Are type-specific agents assigned appropriately?
  - Database stories → @db-sage
  - Frontend stories → @ux-expert
  - Deployment stories → @github-devops
  - Security stories → @architect

**Quality Gate Tasks:**
- Are all applicable quality gates defined as checkboxes?
- Pre-Commit (@dev) - REQUIRED for all stories
- Pre-PR (@github-devops) - Required if PR will be created
- Pre-Deployment (@github-devops) - Required for production stories

**Self-Healing Configuration (Story 6.3.3):**
- Is the self-healing configuration present?
- Does the mode match the primary agent?
  - @dev: light mode (2 iterations, 15 min, CRITICAL only)
  - @qa: full mode (3 iterations, 30 min, CRITICAL+HIGH)
  - @github-devops: check mode (report only)
- Is the severity behavior documented?

**Focus Areas:**
- Do focus areas match the story type?
- Are type-specific validations listed?
  - Database: service filters, schema compliance, RLS
  - API: error handling, security, validation
  - Frontend: accessibility, performance, responsive

**Validation Result:**
- [ ] PASS: CodeRabbit section complete and accurate
- [ ] PARTIAL: Section present but incomplete
- [ ] FAIL: Section missing or critically incomplete
- [ ] N/A: CodeRabbit disabled in core-config.yaml

### 8.1 Code Intelligence: No Duplicate Functionality (Auto-skip if unavailable)

- **Check code intelligence availability:** Call `isCodeIntelAvailable()` from `.aiox-core/core/code-intel`
- **If available:**
  - Call `validateNoDuplicates(storyDescription)` from `.aiox-core/core/code-intel/helpers/story-helper`
    - If `hasDuplicates: true`: Add to validation report as **Should-Fix** issue — "Potential duplicate functionality detected: {suggestion}". This is **advisory only** and does NOT block validation.
    - If `hasDuplicates: false`: Add to report as PASS — "No duplicate functionality detected"
  - Include result in the **Validation Result** section under "Code Intelligence Check"
- **If NOT available:** Skip this step silently — validation proceeds exactly as before with no code intelligence items in report

### 9. Anti-Hallucination Verification

- **Epic Context Enrichment**: Import `EpicContextAccumulator` from `core/orchestration` and call `buildAccumulatedContext(epicId, storyN)` to enrich validation with accumulated epic context (progressive summarization within token limits)
- **Refer to tools/mcp/context7.yaml** for library documentation lookup to verify technical claims against official sources
- Consult the examples section for documentation verification patterns and library-specific queries
- **Source verification**: Every technical claim must be traceable to source documents
- **Architecture alignment**: Dev Notes content matches architecture specifications
- **No invented details**: Flag any technical decisions not supported by source documents
- **Reference accuracy**: Verify all source references are correct and accessible
- **Fact checking**: Cross-reference claims against epic and architecture documents

### 10. Dev Agent Implementation Readiness

- **Self-contained context**: Can the story be implemented without reading external docs?
- **Clear instructions**: Are implementation steps unambiguous?
- **Complete technical context**: Are all required technical details present in Dev Notes?
- **Missing information**: Identify any critical information gaps
- **Actionability**: Are all tasks actionable by a development agent?

### 11. Generate Validation Report

Provide a structured validation report including:

#### Template Compliance Issues

- Missing sections from story template
- Unfilled placeholders or template variables
- Structural formatting issues

#### Critical Issues (Must Fix - Story Blocked)

- Missing essential information for implementation
- Inaccurate or unverifiable technical claims
- Incomplete acceptance criteria coverage
- Missing required sections

#### Should-Fix Issues (Important Quality Improvements)

- Unclear implementation guidance
- Missing security considerations
- Task sequencing problems
- Incomplete testing instructions

#### Nice-to-Have Improvements (Optional Enhancements)

- Additional context that would help implementation
- Clarifications that would improve efficiency
- Documentation improvements

#### Anti-Hallucination Findings

- Unverifiable technical claims
- Missing source references
- Inconsistencies with architecture documents
- Invented libraries, patterns, or standards

#### CodeRabbit Integration Findings (CONDITIONAL)

**IF `coderabbit_integration.enabled: true`:**

- **Story Type Accuracy**: Is the story type correctly classified?
- **Agent Assignment Completeness**: Are all required agents assigned?
- **Quality Gate Coverage**: Are all applicable gates defined?
- **Self-Healing Configuration**: Is Story 6.3.3 configuration present?
- **Focus Areas Relevance**: Do focus areas match story type?

**IF `coderabbit_integration.enabled: false`:**

- **Skip Notice Present**: Verify skip notice is rendered in story
- **No Quality Gate Tasks**: Confirm no CodeRabbit checkboxes exist
- **Manual Review Fallback**: Note that manual review process applies

#### Final Assessment

- **GO**: Story is ready for implementation
- **NO-GO**: Story requires fixes before implementation
- **Implementation Readiness Score**: 1-10 scale
- **Confidence Level**: High/Medium/Low for successful implementation

### 12. Post-Validation Status Update (MANDATORY)

**Reference:** `.claude/rules/story-lifecycle.md` — Draft → Ready transition is @po responsibility.

**This step MUST be executed before presenting results to user.**

**Change Log format:** Use `{date: YYYY-MM-DD}` and `{version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH}`. Version MUST follow semantic bump rules: major for breaking changes, minor for features, patch for fixes/process updates. HALT if either value cannot be resolved deterministically.

#### IF verdict is GO (score >= 7):

0. **Pre-check (blocking):**
   - If current Status is not `**Draft**`, HALT and log: "Cannot apply GO transition: expected Draft, found {current status}."
   - If Change Log section is missing, HALT and request user to restore template structure.
1. **Update story Status field** in the story file: change `**Draft**` to `**Ready**`
2. **Add Change Log entry:**
   ```text
   | {date: YYYY-MM-DD} | {version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH} | Validated GO ({score}/10) — Status: Draft → Ready | @po |
   ```
3. **Log:** "✅ Story status updated: Draft → Ready"

#### IF verdict is NO-GO (score < 7):

0. **Pre-check (blocking):**
   - If current Status is not `**Draft**`, HALT and log: "Cannot apply NO-GO outcome: expected Draft, found {current status}."
   - If Change Log section is missing, HALT and request user to restore template structure.
1. **Keep** story Status as `**Draft**`
2. **Add Change Log entry:**
   ```text
   | {date: YYYY-MM-DD} | {version: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH} | Validation NO-GO — {reason summary} | @po |
   ```
3. **Log:** "❌ Story remains Draft — fixes required before re-validation"

#### Rationale

Status transitions defined in `story-lifecycle.md` are advisory (contextual rules). This step makes them imperative (procedural), ensuring agents always execute the transition as part of the workflow rather than relying on contextual rule awareness.

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to Codex (Codex.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Project "Checks"** is a monorepo containing a React micro-frontend and a Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 backend for the Production Unified Toolkit (PUT) platform at Citibank. It is the centralized orchestration and standardization layer for operational health monitoring, integrating with ITRS, Splunk, Grafana, and AppDynamics without replacing them.

**Key Organizing Principle:** All checks are associated with the Citi System Inventory (CSI) as the primary categorization system.

### Repository Layout

```
put-checks/
├── frontend/        # React 18 + TypeScript MFE (MSW-mocked; Phase 1)
├── backend/         # Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 + Gradle KTS (Phase 2 — in development)
├── docs/            # AIOX stories, specs, architecture
├── PRD.md           # Product Requirements (v2.2)
├── ARCH.md          # Technical Architecture
└── AGENTS.md        # (this file)
```

Almost all FE commands below must be run from `frontend/`. Backend commands run from `backend/`.

## Architecture

### Technology Stack
- **Framework:** React 18 with TypeScript (strict mode)
- **Build Tools:** 
  - Vite for standalone development (`npm run dev`)
  - Webpack with Module Federation for production (`npm run dev:fed`)
- **UI Library:** Material-UI (MUI) v7 with Emotion styling
- **Routing:** React Router v7
- **State Management:** Redux Toolkit + React Context
- **Authentication:** OIDC-React with JWT token handling
- **Testing:** Vitest (unit tests) + Playwright (E2E tests)
- **API Mocking:** Mock Service Worker (MSW) for development

### Deployment Modes
1. **Standalone Mode** (`npm run dev` - port 5173): Full development with welcome page and sidebar
2. **Federated Mode** (`npm run dev:fed` - port 3002): Module Federation integration testing

## Common Development Commands

### Frontend (run from `frontend/`)
```bash
cd frontend/

# Setup
npm install
npm run msw:init

# Development servers
npm run dev              # Webpack/Module Federation (port 3002)
npm run dev:standalone   # Vite standalone (port 5173)

# Quality
npm run type-check
npm run lint
npm run lint:fix

# Tests
npm run test             # Vitest
npm run test:ui
npm run test:e2e         # Playwright
```

### Backend (run from `backend/`)
```bash
cd backend/

./gradlew bootRun        # Spring Boot :8080 (local profile → Zonky embedded Postgres)
./gradlew test           # JUnit 5 + Testcontainers
./gradlew check          # Full build gate (spotless, checkstyle, spotbugs, jacoco)
```

## Development Approach

### Mock-First Development
**CRITICAL:** All API interactions use Mock Service Worker (MSW) during development. This enables:
- Independent frontend development without backend dependency
- Full functionality testing with realistic data
- Stakeholder demos before backend completion

Mock handlers are located in `frontend/src/services/mocks/` and provide realistic API responses for all check types, CSI data, and execution results.

### Module Federation Integration
The module exposes `./ChecksModule` via Module Federation and integrates with the PUT Platform Shell using:
- `PlatformSidebar` from `@put/core-components` for navigation
- Adaptive layouts that detect standalone vs federated deployment
- Event communication with host application

## Key Features and Components

### Core Check Types
1. **Basic Checks:** HTTP/HTTPS endpoints, TCP port connectivity
2. **Integration Checks:** Splunk queries, Grafana metrics, ITRS samplers, AppDynamics health rules
3. **UI Test Checks:** No-code browser automation with "Checks Studio"

### Checks Studio (UI Testing)
**Philosophy:** "From Checklist to Reality" - users write plain English steps and watch video proof of execution.

**Three-Panel Interface:**
- Left: Test steps in numbered list format
- Middle: Control panel with "Run Test" button and live logs
- Right: Video playback synchronized with test steps

### Navigation Structure
```
📁 Checks Module
├── 🏠 Dashboard - Health overview
├── 📋 All Checks - Check management  
├── ➕ Create Check - New check builder
├── 🎬 Checks Studio - UI testing
└── 📊 Reports - Analytics & reporting
```

## Code Organization

```
frontend/src/
├── components/
│   ├── layout/              # Adaptive layouts (LayoutProvider, ChecksLayout)
│   ├── common/              # Shared components
│   └── [features]/          # Feature-specific components
├── pages/                   # Route components
├── store/                   # Redux Toolkit state management
├── services/
│   └── mocks/              # MSW API mocking
├── types/                  # TypeScript definitions
└── utils/                  # Utilities & configuration

backend/src/main/java/com/citi/put/checks/   # bounded contexts (csi, checks, scheduling, …)
backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/     # Flyway forward-only SQL
```

### Environment Configuration
- **Vite dev server** (port 5173) → Standalone mode with full navigation
- **Webpack dev server** (port 3002) → Federated mode for platform integration
- Environment variables in `.env.development` control MSW enablement and API URLs

## Development Rules

### Code Quality
- **TypeScript:** Strict mode enabled, no `any` types without justification
- **Components:** Use MUI components and `sx` prop for styling
- **API Calls:** All HTTP requests through centralized API client, no direct `fetch()`
- **Testing:** Unit tests required for business logic, integration tests for components

### Git Workflow
- **Branching:** Feature branches from `develop` (format: `feat/PROJ-123-description`)
- **Commits:** Follow Conventional Commits specification
- **PRs:** Draft PRs early, squash and merge to maintain clean history

### Authentication & Security
- Enterprise SSO integration via OIDC
- Role-based access control based on CSI ownership
- Secrets vault integration for external system credentials
- No hardcoded credentials or API keys

## Important Files and References

### Primary Documentation
- `PRD.md` - Product requirements and user stories
- `ARCH.md` - Technical architecture and implementation plan
- `MFE_GUIDE.md` - Platform shell implementation details  

### Cursor IDE Rules
- `.cursor/rules/project-overview.mdc` - Project context and verification
- `.cursor/rules/development.mdc` - Git workflow and testing requirements
- `.cursor/rules/frontend-react.mdc` - React/TypeScript development standards

## Performance and Integration

### Bundle Optimization
- Module Federation with shared dependencies (React, MUI, etc.)
- Code splitting and lazy loading
- Target: < 500KB initial bundle, < 1.5s First Contentful Paint

### Platform Communication
- Custom events for module change notifications
- Host application integration via `window.dispatchEvent`
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach

## Testing Philosophy

- **Unit Tests:** Vitest + React Testing Library for components and hooks
- **Integration Tests:** Full user flows with MSW API mocking
- **E2E Tests:** Playwright for critical paths like check creation and execution
- **Mock Data:** Comprehensive test scenarios including error states and edge cases

## Story

As a Studio author, I want to write login steps that reference my saved credentials as `<secret ID>` — exactly as `<var NAME>` works for nonsecret values — and have the guided first Run and later model-free replays fill them only into the one password control at the one moment the step calls for, so that login-protected pages can be tested on the single observed path without any account provider while no credential is ever shown, stored outside Vault, or logged.

## Acceptance Criteria

Binding decisions: login is author-owned through `<secret ID>` steps (design §0); observed/guided is the **only** authoring path and the compile path, artifact 1 and every "legacy" variant are removed by OBS-012A (ADR-SC-005 D-A) — this story therefore has **no legacy half**: one password-only rule, one adapter, one `LOGIN_REQUIRED` signature, two audit paths (`GUIDED`, `OBSERVED_REPLAY`). Binding compliance requirement (design §4.6): secrets stay safe, are used **only at the right moment**, and are **never logged**. Every AC is testable by the oracle it cites (design §7, C-n / SEC-n); security conditions 1–9 (R1-tightened) are carried verbatim.

**Contracts**

1. **AC-1 — v3 contracts and version tuple.** `contracts/v3/` is completed by copy-and-edit from `contracts/v2/` with exactly the design §3 deltas (the existing v3 `result`, `session-view`, `publication-fixtures` are extended, not replaced; `result.schema.json` loses `AWAITING_AUTH`). Structural essentials that a test must falsify: the `authored-inputs` `secretRef` variant has **no `value` property**; `fill.value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}` and the node-free target `{kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}` are permitted only together; `selectOption.value`/`assert.expected` never gain `secretRef`; `observation.coverage.passwordControls` is an integer 0..500 with no name, id, label, value or position; `bridge#dispatch.secret` is a closed object (`secretId`, `value` 1..4096, `versionId` ≤ 256, `allowedOrigins` 1..16 × ≤ 512) present iff the fill value is `secretRef`; `replay-job` gains `secrets`/`secretOrigins` and loses `accountHandle`; `replay-ipc` `Launch3` gains `scope`; `replay-account` is absent; `session`/`session-view`/`commands#start` lose `scope.accountRef`, `authConnection`, `AWAITING_AUTH`; `error`/`result` lose `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` and gain `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `SECRET_USE_REVOKED`, `VAULT_UNAVAILABLE`, `LOGIN_REQUIRED{detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}}`; `clarification` loses `AUTH_REQUIRED`/`CONNECT_ACCOUNT`. Version tuple per design §3 (`contract 3`, `learnedPlan 3`, `observation 3`, `guidedPolicy 3`, `referencePolicy 4`, `lowering 2`, `artifact 3`, `observed-3` language, `observed-4` executor, `observed-replay-3` catalog, `observed-2` validator, `protocol 3`, `replayAuthorization 2`, `accountAbi` removed). Runner `guided/schemas.json`, `guided/types.ts`, `validator/observedSchemas.json`, `executor/observedOperations.ts` and the backend classpath copy are regenerated by `tools/build-studio-observed-schemas.cjs`, never hand-edited; `node tools/check-studio-observed-contracts.cjs` passes. `openapi-v3.yaml` documents the seven public guided routes (`POST /`, `GET /{id}`, `GET /{id}/result`, `GET /{id}/clarification`, `POST /{id}/clarify`, `POST /{id}/cancel`, `POST /{id}/finalize` — the last served by `GuidedPublicationController`) without `accountRef`/`authConnection`; `guided-output-contract.md` states the model may emit the reference, never a literal. The routes stay mounted at `/api/v3` in code; OBS-012A moves them under `/api/v1/studio` in the one public OpenAPI and retires v1/v2 (ADR-SC-005 placement map). Optional top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage:string` is 1..2048 characters, with final UTF-8 diagnostic text at most 2048 bytes, admitted only for an actual consumed failed/uncertain action (`dispatchCount=1`, ledger `FAILED` or `UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`), never `SUCCEEDED`/`OK`. Redact actual resolved and known values before bounding, interpolation, serialization or write. Closed schemas and all owner/fence/context/ledger checks remain; digests, admission, publication and replay authority are unchanged. The existing owner regenerates applicable bundles/classpath and schema/build/reference identities; no new raw-value channel is added. [design §3; §10 row 1; ADR-SC-005 defaults "Contracts", "Public API"] Proposed browser-mode disposition changes only executor/catalog identity in the existing closed tuple; all other tuple members retain their exact current values. No new browser-mode job/configuration field or unsafe alternative is admitted. Generated profileHash/schemaBundleHash/referenceBundleHash, actual executableImageDigest/build, immutable deployment policyVersion and contract/confinement pins are deliberately re-anchored with actual old/new bytes; unavailable image provenance stays NOT_ASSERTED.

2. **AC-2 — Internal `openapi.yaml` closed-schema bump.** `RunnerReport.secretUse: {[secretId]: "USED"|"NOT_USED"|"REFUSED"}` (sparse USED-only on authenticated PROGRESS; USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED on FINAL; unknown omitted, no new field/status) and `ExecutionControl.revoked: boolean` are added per ADR-002 §3.1 (`StrictInternalBodyReader` fails on unknown properties); `x-runner-error-codes` gains `LOGIN_REQUIRED` and `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED`; `InternalBodyContractConformanceTest` parses both new fields. The `x-conflict-codes` entry `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` (`docs/specs/studio/openapi.yaml:256`) is removed in the same edit (no compatibility layer is owed, ADR-SC-005 D-A). `studio-runner/test/run/confinement.test.ts` `BASE_SHA256` and the `StudioContractTest` op-count pin are re-anchored deliberately, old and new values quoted in the Dev Agent Record. [design §3 internal `openapi.yaml` row; security condition 8; oracle C-16; ADR-SC-005 D-A] Positive PROGRESS facts require the exact owner/CAS/frozen-recipe/completed-PASS binding in AC-14. Payload reduction omits unsupported positives; no terminal outcome is placed on PROGRESS. The revised internal description is a semantic contract amendment requiring regenerated identities and quoted pin re-anchors.

**Guided `secretRef` pipeline**

3. **AC-3 — `secretRef` end to end.** A declared `<secret ID>` classifies to `sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:ID}`; an undeclared ID is `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`. The model receives the step text with the token span masked plus the reference (the ID), never a value: a gateway spy asserts the outbound bytes contain the ID and zero planted-value bytes (SEC-1). Materialization adds `authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId}` with no value, hashed into `authoredInputsHash`. The learned plan and lowered artifact carry `fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}` and `inputRecipes[inputId]={kind:secretRef, referenceName:ID}` — the **only** spelling of a secret use on the single path — and `artifactHash` is identical before and after a Vault rotation (SEC-8). `validator/observedReplay.ts` and `ObservedRevisionVerifier` refuse any artifact whose fill literal equals a declared secret's resolved value and any `authoredLiteral`/`sourceSpan` overlapping a `<secret …>` token. [design §2, §3 "Reference rule"]

4. **AC-4 — Right moment: step binding (I-A1).** A secret is filled only (a) at a step whose authored source declares it, (b) in slot `fill.value`, (c) into the unique password control of AC-5, (d) on an origin in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins` whose owning `form.action` origin is inside `allowedOrigins`. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts a `passwordControl` target only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; `executionEvidence` document/generation staleness checks are unchanged. Runner `guided/runtime.ts` insists `input.sourceStepId === coordinate.stepId && intendedSlot === slot` for `secretRef` as it does for `authoredLiteral`; `validator/observedReplay.ts` and the observed executor re-check `inputRecipes[].stepId` at validation and at `perform` (`REFERENCE_MISMATCH`). The artifact-1 binding in `validator/references.ts` is **not** cited as evidence (it leaves with OBS-012A). [design §4.6 I-A1; §4.2; §4.3; oracle C-1]

5. **AC-5 — Trusted password-control resolution (security condition 1, tightened by R1-1/R1-2/R1-3).** The model never sees a password node (the collector does not export them). "Visible, enabled `input[type=password]`" is defined **once** in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots, frames and closed shadow roots excluded — and that single function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll('input[type=password]')` resolver outside it is forbidden (static test, C-20). Resolution runs inside the collector's isolated world under the existing `acquire`-style guard (cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call); the element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world and the fill requires the **same element** still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique candidate, with `location.origin` read in-world (not `page.url()`) inside `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill (C-18). 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing typed; off-screen rendered decoys count (⇒ refuse), iframe/closed-shadow inputs do not (⇒ absent ⇒ refuse). A pinned input whose owning `form.action` resolves to an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or a form-less input on a document whose origin differs from the observed login document, ⇒ `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`, nothing typed (C-19). **Limit (ADR-SC-005 default, no opt-out):** multi-password pages and secrets into non-password controls are unsupported for `secretRef` fills at GA — `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`/`POLICY_DENIED`, nothing typed, no fallback adapter; stated in the runner README. [design §4.2, §4.3; security review "R1 delta check" R1-1, R1-2, R1-3; oracles SEC-6, C-18, C-19, C-20; ADR-SC-005 defaults "Secrets"]

6. **AC-6 — Just-in-time delivery, scoping, digests (I-A2, I-A3, F-7, F-10).** Backend `mayUse` is checked at session start (names only, before any browser; `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, zero Vault reads, no session row), at `prepareAndAdmit` (names only) and at dispatch (`resolve` + erase), through `VaultStudioReferenceResolver` with `VaultScope.of(csiId, environmentId, testId)` and the Run principal; a same-named secret under another CSI is `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, never the other value (SEC-2). The value travels only in the `BridgeDispatch.secret` of the admitted fill, built after `consume()` commits inside the resolution scope, never journaled, never in a retry buffer or idempotency store (C-2: exactly one `dispatch` frame carries it; no `context`/`prepare`/`observe`/`stop` frame does). The backend dispatch digest is computed without `secret`; the runner replay map strips `secret` before hashing — byte-identical bodies differing only in `secret.value` yield the same digest, a different `secret.secretId` yields `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` (C-15). The runner `withhold`s the value before the fill and drops the frame reference; `knownSecrets` scrubs any echo from the next observation (SEC-4 `/echo`); inventory and `knownSecrets` are wiped at `dispose()` and on `stop` (SEC-3). The guided mode asserts `capacity === 1` while secret fills are enabled (`CONFIGURATION_DENIED` otherwise) **or** a two-session cross-value isolation oracle passes — the implemented choice is stated in evidence (C-17). Observed replay keeps run-scoped delivery (all declared secrets resolved once at dispatch; per-step delivery rejected, design I-A2). [design §4.4, §4.6 I-A2/I-A3; F-7; F-10; security conditions 7, 9]

**Observed replay**

7. **AC-7 — Replay secrets through the ordinary dispatch pass.** Observed replay carries `job.secrets`/`job.secretOrigins`, resolved per run inside `ObservedReplayAuthorization.job()` within the ordinary dispatch pass; `Launch3` carries `scope` instead of deriving it from an account handle; the observed adapter performs the same origin check (`secretOrigins` per ID; absent list ⇒ bound to no origin) and the same password-only rule — the published `passwordControl` guard replayed against `/two-passwords` or `/no-password` ⇒ `POLICY_REFUSED`, nothing typed; replay is model-free (both gateways silent). The `requireSecretOrigin` implementation in `playwrightAdapter.ts` is **not** what the test cites (removed by OBS-012A). [design §3 `replay-job`/`replay-ipc` rows, §4.3, §4.6 I-A2/I-A3; oracle SEC-6 replay row, C-1]

8. **AC-8 — No value reads on password controls (F-6).** `hasValue`/`controlValue` reads on `type=password` controls are refused in the observed executor (learn and replay) with `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED`; assertion failure text never embeds a password-control reading (`observed` omitted); a deliberately failing value assertion on a text control whose page shows the canary produces redacted failure text (C-14). [design §4.6 I-B5; security condition 6]

**Never logged — sink inventory**

9. **AC-9 — Backend sinks (I-B4, F-4).** A final `SecretValue` type wraps `char[]`, prints `<secret>` from `toString()`, has no Jackson-visible getter and is written only by one explicit writer (`JsonGenerator.writeString(char[],int,int)`) used by the two secret-bearing serializers (`HttpRunnerDispatchClient` body, guided `BridgeDispatch` builder) and replay `job()`, erasing after write; `RunJob.resolvedSecrets: Map<String,String>` and `text(resolved.secrets())` are replaced. The Vault read is parsed with a streaming `JsonParser` (`getTextCharacters`) straight into `char[]` — the secret path never calls `ObjectMapper.readTree`; bodies are published as `byte[]` (`ofByteArray`) and zeroed after send (test seams for both). Oracle C-5: with root and `com.citi.put.checks` at TRACE and every appender captured during a two-path controlled run (guided learn, observed replay), zero canary hits in logs, problem+json bodies, SSE frames, `/actuator/prometheus` and the `IdempotencyFilter` cache; `RunJob.toString()`/`SecretValue.toString()` print no value. Residuals (JVM `String` copies, Jackson/`HttpClient`/TLS buffers) are documented in the evidence file, not asserted. [design §4.6 I-B4, I-A2 read/write residuals; security condition 4]

10. **AC-10 — Runner sinks (I-B5, SEC-7, F-10).** A static test asserts `tracing.start`, `recordHar`, `on('console'` and `screenshot` stay absent from `studio-runner/src`. The guided mode runs a redactor built from the resolved values over stderr lines, journal diagnostic text and callback `errorMessage` (a test-only hook embedding the value yields `[REDACTED]`, SEC-7). Oracle C-6 uses the separately labeled mandatory native, injected and supplementary controls below. Callback free text is exactly top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage`; journal free text is a distinct per-session diagnostic JSONL file with a closed safe identity plus already-redacted text. `GuidedJournal` keeps its existing owner/consumption hashes. The separate diagnostic file has restrictive permissions and finite session record/byte budgets; consume/recovery never reads it, it cannot restore/retry/admit/publish, and diagnostic-write failure cannot change a determined verdict or completed success. Redact actual resolved/known values before truncation, interpolation, serialization, stderr, callback or file write, then enforce the character and UTF-8 bounds; never stringify a secret-bearing frame or raw exception wholesale. C-6 separates three mandatory controls. Authentic production failures/refusals execute through the sole isolated collector/CDP password primitive, privately capturing actual raw text at the declared volatile test seam; the current trusted native refusal is asserted code-only TARGET_CHANGED without released-canary content. Supplementary direct Playwright.fill /slow timeout retains every raw-canary-positive, safe-[REDACTED]-positive and no-canary assertion. The injected actual released-value Error executes the production GuidedRuntime diagnostics and proves redaction before interpolation/bounds, UTF-8/character and session budgets, callback/sidecar/stderr scrubbing and unchanged hash-only GuidedJournal. Native, injected and supplementary evidence are labeled independently and cannot substitute for each other. Actual sole-primitive in-flight timeout, cancellation and context/transport loss exercise truthful effect knowledge; a readonly prewrite refusal alone is not a timeout proof. For the actual Core-HTTP/PostgreSQL/compiled-child/browser join require zero literal/encoded canary hits in child stdout/stderr, relay output, step failure, manifest, callbacks, diagnostic journal, authoritative journal and parent log for all applicable controls; constructionally discarded output is verified as discarded at its actual boundary, never credited as a redactor output that was not produced. Parent DEBUG=pw:* remains absent from the child environment while the run proceeds. No second selector/fill/raw-value production channel is added. The original literal positive assertion that an authentic production password native raw error contains the released canary remains preserved as historically unmet; only explicit independent PO revalidation of this exact replacement supersedes it. All other historical native/injected/supplementary assertions, negative/positive cases and complete sink scans remain mandatory. Code-only native text alone, an injected hook, absent sink or a unit redactor does not close the joined C-6 oracle. [design §4 "Runner outputs", §4.6 I-B5; security condition 9]

11. **AC-11 — Browser profile disk sink (F-3).** Both guided and observed-replay modes use one fixed bundled full Chromium new-headless runtime (Playwright channel=chromium, headless=true, chromiumSandbox=true, explicit args=[]), never configurable shell/branded/system executable fallback. At the investigated pin this is Playwright1.63.0/Chromium153.0.8010.12; retain the exact browser revision and executable/image identity as build evidence. Each persistent context has a fresh confined per-session/per-run user-data directory with prewritten Default/Preferences before launch, containing registered supported preferences credentials_enable_service=false (password-save control), autofill.profile_enabled=false, autofill.credit_card_enabled=false and session.restore_on_startup=5. Refuse missing, malformed or unsafe prepared preferences before launch (negative tests). Verify the actual selected executable, active Default profile confinement and all four effective registered preferences in the exact sandboxed owned browser/image lane; no literal verifiedPreferences=true substitutes. The unsupported legacy profile.password_manager_enabled key is not an effective assertion for this pinned build; retain historical unmet legacy-effective assertions explicitly, with supersession only after PO approval. ### What the code does today (design §1, condensed)

Guided input kinds are `nonsecretText | destination` and require a value. `GuidedSourceClassifier` already parses `<secret ID>` and requires it declared but emits configuration references only for `var`; the change is emission, not parsing. Every guided start fails `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED`. `knownSecrets` is always `[]`; the collector merges/withholds and wipes on dispose; sanitizer bound 64 × 4096. The collector **never exports a password control as a node** — hence the node-free target. The ordinary dispatch pass resolves secrets at dispatch only, erases on every exit path, carries `secretOrigins`; it has no password-only rule and no login detection. The observed replay job carries `accountHandle`; V33 DB functions require account fields; `AWAITING_AUTH` is in the V30 CHECK. `translation.enabled` is dead unless set (two gates). No production guided data exists; publication and observed replay default off; the guided worker has no `CMD`/chart (OBS-009).

### Target flow (design §2)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports"
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight mayUse + exists, no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS} (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target={kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner pins exactly one visible enabled input[type=password]
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal), RELEASE audit row, BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → same pinned element re-proven in-world (attached, type=password, unique, origin, form.action), withhold BEFORE fill, fill via handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run (ordinary dispatch pass), same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```

### Trust boundaries in one paragraph (design §4)

The gateway sees IDs, never values (structural: the kind has no `value` field). The DB stores IDs, vault version identifiers and audit rows. The only value-bearing channels are `BridgeDispatch.secret` (guided, mTLS + RS256) and `Launch3/Execute3.secrets` (replay, the backend→runner hop that OBS-009 makes TLS with client-certificate authentication). Runner memory holds the value from the dispatch frame until `withhold` copies it into the private inventory; wiped at `dispose`/`stop`; no scratch file, argv or env ever carries it. The browser profile is a separate disk sink neutralised by the pre-written `Preferences` file and canary-scanned. Video shows masked dots only (password-only rule); a page that later echoes a secret in plain text is a stated residual. Runner free-text sinks pass a redactor built from resolved values. Transport gates G-1 (guided mTLS), G-2 (no real credential in Vault until every secret-bearing hop is TLS-authenticated) and G-3 (no scheduled secret-referencing run before production background/secret-use authorization sources exist) are OBS-009/OBS-010 items and are **not** closed by this story.

13. **AC-13 — No stale frame; bounded post-release window; revocation (I-A3, F-2).** The verified dispatch ordering is preserved: resolve immediately before `send`; `AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED` closes with no send; a Vault outage releases the claim and the next pass re-resolves; a retryable definite refusal re-queues with a fresh `attempt_id` and re-resolves; an ambiguous send is never resent; Guided recovery has three real fault positions: live/fresh same-worker/context/proof `ADMITTED/count0` before consume starts reads0/sends0 and may win consume once, recheck current authorization/origin/evidence, resolve once and send at most once; committed consume/count1 before resolve yields `AlreadyConsumed` with zero reads/sends and no new read/resend; after actual resolve or ambiguous send recovery adds no read/send, erases transient scope, preserves known success/failure and records honest uncertainty for unobserved effects. Context loss cannot rebuild/replay a browser; no `WonConsumption`, value or frame is cached, and no read-and-discard manufactures a counter. Ordinary observed replay Vault-outage/new-read and definite-refusal/fresh-`attempt_id`/fresh-resolution proof remain unchanged, including revocation between passes, the real read-counter assertion and unreachable old `RunJob`. C-5 TRACE every appender and API/SSE/metrics/idempotency scan still spans those C-4 sub-runs. New: a worker-side revocation sweep rechecks `mayUse` for every in-flight execution/session holding a released secret at the control-poll cadence and writes a write-once `revoked_at`; `ExecutionControl.revoked` is carried on the progress acknowledgement by the same path as `cancelRequested`; guided sessions receive `stop{reason: REVOKED}`; the run cancels within one control poll (bound stated as ≤ 2 s plus one in-flight step, never zero) with nothing typed and an audit row `REVOKED_MID_RUN`. Missing trusted facts/control-network loss stay unmapped cancellation/uncertainty, with no invented cause. Completed `PASSED`, `FAILED`, assertion-failure and `LOGIN_REQUIRED` outcomes are never rewritten by later facts. Keep write-once `revoked_at`, unique `REVOKED_MID_RUN`, worst-phase/slow/lost-response proof and the ≤2 s including request/queue time plus one already-in-flight step residual, with no next-step typing. # Secret-reference login in guided runs — technical design

Status: **R3 — canonical design for secret-reference login on the single observed path ([ADR-SC-005](../../architecture/ADR-SC-005-single-path-observed-authoring.md)).** Written by Aria (@architect), 2026-10-09; R3 the same day after the user accepted the single-path ruling. Design only: no code, schema, migration, OpenAPI, test or story file is changed by this document. Every `path:line` below was read on this working tree on 2026-10-09 (HEAD `d954a21c5`); line numbers drift. R3 removes every legacy-compile-path variant (the compile path is retired by STUDIO-OBS-012A): the password-only rule has one adapter and no opt-out; `LOGIN_REQUIRED` is computed from the observation signature on both guided learn and observed replay; migrations follow the ADR-SC-005 D-B re-baseline (V34 absorbed); the backend→runner hop is one TLS/client-certificate hop to one runner process; §10 maps items onto the ADR-SC-005 story set. Incremental re-learn (ADR-SC-005 D-D) does not change this design: a `secretRef` fill in a reused prefix step is replayed by the observed adapter under the same rules.

## 0. Decision record

If a step uses a login-protected page, the author writes login steps before it and references credentials as `<secret ID>` exactly the way nonsecret values use `<var NAME>`. There is **no** external account/session provider, **no** same-session sign-in handoff, **no** account-selection UI. EXT-001 is dropped. |

## 2. Target flow (one page)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports" / …
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight(mayUse + exists), no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS}  (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value = {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target = {kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}  (node-free: the collector never exports a password node)
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner proves exactly one visible enabled input[type=password] in the current top-level document
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal scope), RELEASE audit row, send BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → trusted runner re-resolves that unique password input at fill time (0 or >1 ⇒ POLICY_DENIED), origin ∈ allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins, withhold(value) BEFORE fill, fill via the pinned handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run by the ordinary dispatch pass, same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```

## 4. Trust boundaries, value lifetime, password-only ruling

| Boundary | Rule |
|---|---|
| Gateway (model) | Receives step text with the `<secret ID>` span masked plus the reference `{kind:secretRef, referenceName:ID}`. The ID is permitted (GA plan §7 AC-1); the value is structurally impossible (no `value` field on the kind). Outgoing-bytes canary test. |
| Backend DB | Stores only IDs, vault **version identifiers** and audit rows (§4.1). The dispatch frame is assembled after `GuidedSessionService.consume()` commits (`GuidedDispatchService.java:80-100`) and is never journaled; `Resolved` is try-with-resources (`StudioReferenceResolver.Resolved.close()`). |
| Controller → runner bridge | The only channels carrying a value: `BridgeDispatch.secret` (guided, on the mTLS + RS256 JWT chain — `GuidedInternalSecurity.java`, `guided/transport.ts:59-61`) and the `/v2/runs` job → `Launch3/Execute3.secrets` (replay, on the backend→runner hop, which becomes TLS with client-certificate authentication of the backend under Q4/G-2; today plaintext `node:http` with a static bearer, `server.ts:17,33`). One runner process serves both listeners' routes (ADR-SC-005 default). Closed key sets; schema-validated before send and on receipt. |
| Runner memory | Value lives in the dispatch frame until `withhold([value])` copies it into the collector's private inventory (`browser.ts:335`), then the frame reference is dropped. Inventory wiped at `dispose()` (`browser.ts:452`) and on `stop`. The runner itself writes no scratch file, argv or env with a value (legacy rule, `protocol.ts:106`); the browser profile is a separate sink, next row. |
| Browser profile (disk, F-3) | Both guided and observed-replay modes use one fixed bundled full Chromium new-headless runtime (Playwright channel=chromium, headless=true, chromiumSandbox=true, explicit args=[]), never configurable shell/branded/system executable fallback. At the investigated pin this is Playwright1.63.0/Chromium153.0.8010.12; retain the exact browser revision and executable/image identity as build evidence. Each persistent context has a fresh confined per-session/per-run user-data directory with prewritten Default/Preferences before launch, containing registered supported preferences credentials_enable_service=false (password-save control), autofill.profile_enabled=false, autofill.credit_card_enabled=false and session.restore_on_startup=5. Refuse missing, malformed or unsafe prepared preferences before launch (negative tests). Verify the actual selected executable, active Default profile confinement and all four effective registered preferences in the exact sandboxed owned browser/image lane; no literal verifiedPreferences=true substitutes. The unsupported legacy profile.password_manager_enabled key is not an effective assertion for this pinned build; retain historical unmet legacy-effective assertions explicitly, with supersession only after PO approval. It may remain inert prepared metadata, never security evidence. The fixed browser-save policy plus fresh-profile isolation replaces that obsolete effective-key claim, without claiming credential autofill is disabled by credentials_enable_service alone. After a login that would otherwise offer password saving, canary-scan the complete recorded and guided profile/user-data scratch trees before context close/clear, requiring zero hits. Preserve no extra browser args, sandbox/confinement, child environment allowlist, downloads/network/privacy restrictions and cleanup. State transient cache/session-file residuals. OBS-013 still adds recording of this same guided context; manual video masking remains OBS-009. Re-anchor the runtime/profile/policy/catalog identities under the approved mode change; no obsolete identity or image-provenance reuse. |
| Runner outputs | Authority-bearing ledger/observation and GuidedJournal records retain closed safe metadata. Callback free text is exactly top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage`; journal free text is a distinct per-session diagnostic JSONL file with a closed safe identity plus already-redacted text. `GuidedJournal` keeps its existing owner/consumption hashes. The separate diagnostic file has restrictive permissions and finite session record/byte budgets; consume/recovery never reads it, it cannot restore/retry/admit/publish, and diagnostic-write failure cannot change a determined verdict or completed success. Redact actual resolved/known values before truncation, interpolation, serialization, stderr, callback or file write, then enforce the character and UTF-8 bounds; never stringify a secret-bearing frame or raw exception wholesale. Optional top-level `BridgeOutcome.errorMessage:string` is 1..2048 characters, with final UTF-8 diagnostic text at most 2048 bytes, admitted only for an actual consumed failed/uncertain action (`dispatchCount=1`, ledger `FAILED` or `UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`), never `SUCCEEDED`/`OK`. Redact actual resolved and known values before bounding, interpolation, serialization or write. Closed schemas and all owner/fence/context/ledger checks remain; digests, admission, publication and replay authority are unchanged. The existing owner regenerates applicable bundles/classpath and schema/build/reference identities; no new raw-value channel is added. Native capture is test-only volatile memory, never a raw production channel. |
| Video | Masked dots only, because of the password-only rule below. Disclosed as a separate channel; a secret filled into a page that later echoes it in plain text is **not** protected by video and is recorded as a known residual. |
