## Decision

UI Studio is unreleased. It ships **one** authoring path, production-ready end to end, with no legacy path, no compatibility layer and no versioned fallback.

**D-A — Observed/guided is the only authoring path; compile-to-READY is removed entirely.** The author writes plain English and presses Run. The first Run learns while acting against sanitized observations of the live page (accessibility/semantic nodes, bounded DOM neighbourhood, never raw HTML, password controls withheld), publishes the exact exercised plan, and later Runs replay it model-free. The compile pipeline (`studio/compile/**`), the artifact-1 TypeScript engine in the runner (`validator/{ast,arguments,language,references,referencePolicy,schema}.ts`, `executor/{operations,executor}.ts`, `run/playwrightAdapter.ts`), the runner routes `/v1/validate` and `/v1/runs`, the public routes `compile` and `confirm-compile`, the compile UI (`components/studio/review/**`, `CodeTab`, `inference/**`, `features/studio/authoring/**`) and the compile pins (`studio.runtime.pin.*`) are deleted. Compile concepts survive only inside the observed path: pre-browser validation (`GuidedProposalValidator`, `/v2/validate-observed`), bounded schema repair, `CredentialPatternScreen` (already wired in `GuidedSourceClassifier:24-29`), and the shared gateway pieces, which move out of `compile/` into a neutral `studio/gateway` package: `GenAiGatewayTransport`, `StudioGatewayConfig`/`Properties`, `BudgetedAuthTransport`, `BoundedCredentialProvider`, `GatewayAudit*`, `ErrorScrubber`, `FailureClassifier`, `PayloadSerializer`, `Provenance` (≈1,580 LOC, panel dev). `compile/validator/StudioRunnerProperties` moves to the dispatch/runner client package.

**D-B — Migrations re-baselined (pre-release exception to `ARCH.md:123`).** Checks core V1–V11 stay byte-identical. Studio V12–V33 and `backend/db/cutover/V19` are re-authored as seven area migrations, absorbing the planned V34: `V12__tests_revisions`, `V13__executions_ledger`, `V14__guided_sessions`, `V15__publication`, `V16__scheduling`, `V17__secret_use_audit`, `V18__drop_plaintext_secrets` (@data-engineer option A; today's V25 becomes V18). Compile-only state is not carried: `ui_tests` compile columns (V12/V16/V18/V21), `ui_test_revisions` compile identity (V18/V21/V22–V24/V29), `ui_test_step_identities`, `ui_test_compile_requests`, `ui_test_compile_outcomes` (V18), and the V19 cutover. Evidence that no shared environment has ever been deployed: `helm-chart/put-checks/values.yaml:96`, `docs/epics/EPIC-10-EXECUTION.yaml:66-67`, `staging-acceptance-register.md:250`, `docs/runbooks/studio-inference-rollout.md:102` (panel devops). **Residual:** only the user or Platform/SRE can confirm that nothing was ever deployed from an internal remote; this ADR records that confirmation as owed, not obtained. Consequences: dev databases are recreated; the 17 integration tests pinned to Flyway targets are rewritten; Hibernate entities change in the same change.

**D-C — Pilot gate: real-model guided benchmark.** Before any human pilot: ≥ 20 workflows (the 13 compile benchmark cases ported, plus login and multi-step dataflow) × 3 real-model repetitions on the deployed stack with pinned model/prompt/runtime versions; ≥ 90% end-to-end completion without clarification on unambiguous cases; **zero false passes and zero secret/PII leaks are hard gates**; p50/p95 latency, model calls, tokens and configured-provider cost per run are published with denominators. The corpus includes at least two incremental cases (edit step 4 of 10; insert a step) proving that exactly steps k…n were re-learned and 1…k-1 produced zero model calls (D-D). No real-model evidence for guided exists today (`GuidedProviderEvaluationTest.java:58-84` skips `UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN`; OBS-006 `review-record.json:259`).

**D-D — GA supports incremental re-learn from the first changed step** (user correction 2026-10-09, binding: "in case we have a 10-step test and we change step 4, only step 4 and beyond (5..10) should be regenerated"). The STUDIO-INC-001 incremental requirement carries over to the observed path. Each published learned plan is an immutable per-step snapshot (revision) with per-step hashes. On edit, the first changed step **k** is the first index whose authored text, referenced variable/secret declarations or step-level configuration differs from the published revision; inserts, deletes and reorders count at the first affected index; multiple edits take the earliest. The next Run replays steps 1…k-1 from the published plan model-free (fresh values recaptured, same drift refusals), switches to learning at step k through the end, and publishes a new revision = reused prefix 1…k-1 + newly learned k…n. Steps after k are **always** re-learned even when their text is unchanged (page state and dataflow may differ). The UX statement is: **"Learn again" re-learns from the first changed or drifted step, not the whole test.** Rules: no edit since the last publish → plain replay; first ever Run → full learn; a test-level configuration change (environment, approved origins, viewport, timeout, browser) → k = 1. Defaults stated by the user and adopted: bindings produced in 1…k-1 are recaptured during prefix replay and are available to k…n planning under their existing server-issued IDs; SOURCE_PLAN for the suffix sees the full checklist but plans only k…n; if prefix replay drifts at step j < k the session continues in learning mode from j and the user is told "steps j… were re-learned because the page changed". **Architect conditions on that last default (flagged, not a disagreement with intent):** (1) only target/observation drift (`TARGET_DRIFT`, locator ambiguity, stale generation) may switch to learning; an assertion `FAIL` or `POLICY_REFUSED` in the prefix stops the run, because re-interpreting a failing check or a refused action is not what the author asked for; (2) the switch point j is recorded in the receipt and the published revision marks steps j…k-1 as re-learned, not reused; (3) prefix actions already dispatched are never repeated (at-most-once stands); (4) steps j…k-1 charge the same session model budget. Implementation is **STUDIO-OBS-015, in the GA wave**; see the placement map for the contract change.

**Defaults accepted by the user (2026-10-09):**

| Default | Decision |
|---|---|
| Runner topology | One runner process, image and Deployment; the guided worker becomes a mode of the main runner (`guidedMain.ts` is a 33-line bootstrap of `createGuidedServer`). One TLS listener with client-certificate authentication of the backend serves `/v2/runs`, `/v2/validate-observed` and the guided-session bridge |
| Public API | Guided-session routes live under `/api/v1/studio/guided-sessions` in the one public OpenAPI document (`docs/specs/studio/openapi.yaml`); `/api/v3` is not used |
| Secrets | Multi-password pages are unsupported for `secretRef` fills at GA (`PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing typed); the password-only rule has no opt-out |
| Contracts | One contract version, `contracts/v3`; the nine-pin `versions` tuple plus profile catalog collapses to `{contract: 3, build}` with the build identity `assertBuild` already checks |
| Readiness vocabulary | `UNLEARNED \| LEARNING \| READY \| NEEDS_RELEARN`; `NEEDS_RELEARN` carries `firstChangedStepId` (D-D); `409 LEARN_REQUIRED` replaces `COMPILE_REQUIRED`; `confirmation_source` is `GUIDED_RUN` only |
| Flags | `studio.guided-authoring.translation.enabled` gets an explicit on-by-default (today `@ConditionalOnProperty(havingValue="true")` with no `matchIfMissing`, so the only path is dead unless set); `allowAuthoredNonsecret=true` (INPUT-POLICY-01 branch A, approved); `studio.guided.publication.enabled` and `studio.observed-replay.enabled` default on; `studio.execution.enabled` remains the kill switch |

## Panel evidence (2026-10-09)

1. **Architect.** The compile benchmark (`docs/stories/UI-STUDIO-VALIDATION-20261004/benchmark/report.md`) is NEEDS_WORK and its unsolved class is structural (C07 scored 0 under every config: `searchbox` guessed for a `combobox`). Observed proposals choose from observed nodes and the runner refuses dispatch unless the durable locator resolves to the same element — addressed by construction, accuracy unmeasured. Runtime dataflow exists only on observed. Replay is model-free. Cost envelope: 600 s / 100 proposals / 128k+32k tokens per session; 60 s and 4096 output tokens per call (`GuidedSessionProperties`, `GuidedTranslationProperties`). Operational debt: no guided Dockerfile CMD or Helm template; `mtls-required` defaults false and fails closed; `@Profile("!worker")` on `ObservedReplayConfiguration`/`GuidedPublicationConfiguration` leaves worker pods without the observed verifier (`ExecutionReadinessService.java:124-128,264-268`; `StudioDispatcher.java:79,277,388`).
2. **QA (ran on `d954a21c5`).** Backend guided: 26 classes / 482 tests / 0 failures / 1 skip (`GuidedProviderEvaluationTest`, no env), 8 m 19 s. Runner guided/observed: 13 files / 318 pass; real-Chromium guided/observed fixtures 7 files / 152 pass; contract checker PASS; SDC preflight 32/32. Proven in controlled joined integration (real backend + PostgreSQL + guided worker + Chromium): observe → translate (controlled provider) → act → clarify → publish → model-free replay ×2 with video `AVAILABLE` and a 206 range read (`GuidedPublicationReplayIT:680-907`). **Not proven:** any real LLM on guided; enterprise pages (SSO, shadow DOM, iframes, virtualised lists); worker-profile dispatch (no test); deployability; scheduling; login; UI; public-HTTP mid-step cancel of a live guided browser. `translation.enabled` has no default. Sleep-polled ITs of 54–126 s are flake exposure.
3. **Security.** Verified bounds: admitted obligations, author-bound navigate, values never through the model, targets re-acquired before dispatch, password rule. Residuals: **HIGH** un-requested side-effecting clicks — `targetIntent` is model-chosen and the validator checks structure, not correspondence to authored words; MEDIUM same-origin exfiltration; MEDIUM clarification labels are page-derived. LLM boundary: control names/headings/links exported under `allowStructuralDiscovery` can carry PII; the read/discovery policy is one worker-mounted file per deployment (`guidedMain.ts:18-20`) with no owner, approval or audit; the DB persists sanitized observations (`studio_guided_sessions.progress`) and model output (`studio_guided_model_attempts.safe_result`); gateway retention is unknown. Removing the compile path removes the `/v1` goto-anything executor (net SSRF reduction).
4. **UX.** The guided worker records **no video** (grep `video` in `studio-runner/src/guided` → 0; the runbook defers the first guided recording) — a product-thesis gap. The start command has no from-step parameter. First-Run latency is minutes (p95 18 s per call). OBS-008 should split into transport/states/login, references/capability, and compile-UI removal + vocabulary; the full state model with copy is in the UX report handed to @sm.
5. **Dev.** Code health C+. Compile removal ≈ 55–60k lines (~30k JSON fixtures); guided v1 collapse ≈ 19k lines plus 36 ITs ported. Shared gateway ≈ 1,580 LOC must leave `compile/`. Duplicated families to fold: `GuidedRunnerClient`/`ObservedValidationClient` into the dispatch client; `GuidedPublicationAuthorization` into `DispatchAuthorization`; guided worker into the main runner. `GuidedSessionService.claim()` is 606 lines, `checkCommand` 365; runner guided TypeScript is minified-style (lines to 792 chars); 11.3k generated lines are checked in beside their generator; `GuidedSessionReaper`/`GuidedTranslationCoordinator` are `@Scheduled` with no profile gate (inferred: run on every API replica).
6. **Data engineer.** Option A as in D-B. `ui_tests`/`ui_test_executions` are core (V1) and stay. V25 drops the core `secrets` table from inside the Studio range and becomes V18.
7. **DevOps.** No shared environment ever deployed; no CI; personal remote; no external contract consumers (ROD 9.6 Draft targets core APIs).

## Consequences

**Architecture (one path).** MFE `Run` → `GET /tests/{id}` readiness → `POST guided-sessions` (learn) or `POST /tests/{id}/execute` (replay). Learn: SOURCE_PLAN → materialize inputs (`var`/`secretRef`, no values) → assign worker → per action: observe → NEXT_ACTION → validate → prepare/pin → admit → dispatch once → outcome; one clarification on ambiguity; `secretRef` fills resolve from Vault at dispatch into the unique password control and are erased; FINALIZING → client finalize → exact plan → pure validation → Core authorization → revision (`GUIDED_RUN`) + receipt. Replay: acceptance → readiness (observed verifier) → ledger → `/v2/runs` → recorded child + observed adapter, zero gateway calls; drift stops at step N, and "Learn again" starts a mixed-mode session that replays 1…N-1 and learns from N. Incremental re-learn (D-D): `NEEDS_RELEARN{firstChangedStepId: k}` → Run starts a mixed-mode guided session with `baseRevisionId` → `REPLAYING_PREFIX` (observed adapter, model-free, bindings recaptured) → learning from k → publication merges reused prefix snapshots with newly learned steps. Evidence: webm + manifest to Sonic, step offsets for seek, SSE snapshots — **for the first Run too** (STUDIO-OBS-013; today absent).

**Removed / moved / kept** — the architect's keep/remove table (backend, runner, frontend, contracts, migrations, config, docs) is binding; summary: remove compile pipeline and UI, artifact-1 engine, `/v1/*` runner routes, compile public routes, `studio.compile.**`, `studio.authoring.v2-enabled`, `studio.runtime.pin`, guided v1/v2 contract generations and `observed-1`, dual `/internal/v1|v2` mount (`GuidedInternalController.java:17-20`), account-provider machinery, T-INC deferrals (`InferenceStudio`, `compile/incremental`, V2-engine methods, `EvidenceReference` DTO, V19 cutover). Keep readiness/acceptance/dispatch/ledger/admission, secrets, scheduling, evidence, SSE, `RunControl`/`useRunGate` (re-pointed), evidence/seek, lists, scheduling UI, `SecretInput`.

**Contracts and pins.** `contracts/v3` only; one public OpenAPI; one `BASE_SHA256` over the whole public document (`studio-runner/test/run/confinement.test.ts`); `StudioContractTest` op-count over surviving operations; `tools/check-studio-observed-contracts.cjs` reads v3 only; `tools/build-studio-observed-schemas.cjs` regenerates runner/backend bundles from v3 with a CI check that regeneration is byte-identical; `GuidedSessionIT`, `GuidedHttpSecurityIT`, `GuidedBridgeIntegrationTest` ported to v3; `NoRuntimeLlmTest` keeps the authoring-only gateway allowance with the compile edge deleted; `DeReadyCarryForwardTest` asserts zero guided calls through replay.

**Security work becomes stories.** P0 (STUDIO-OBS-014 unless external): compliance approval of page-metadata/origin export and retention of sanitized observations and model output (external approval, recorded as a release gate in OBS-010); per-application read/discovery policy as a governed object (CSI-owner owned, Security-approved, versioned, audited) replacing the single mounted file; SEC-4 provisioning (OBS-009). P1 (OBS-014): semantic grounding of click/press/check `targetIntent` to authored text; destructive-verb guard; first-Run side-effect policy; clarification choices carry `labelSource` so the UI (OBS-008) marks page-derived labels untrusted; guided session start classified `EXECUTE` in `RateLimitClassifier.java:31-35` plus per-CSI concurrent-session and daily-token budgets; replay execute requires `Idempotency-Key`; per-action audit to SIEM. P2: artifact HMAC with a key outside the DB.

**Operations.** One runner image/Deployment with a guided mode; mTLS chain provisioned (G-1); backend→runner hop TLS with client certificate (G-2); `@Scheduled` guided beans profile-gated; dumps disabled; Vault least privilege; observed schedules lifted behind G-3 (OBS-009). Dev databases recreated after D-B; runbook row (OBS-010).

**Tests.** Compile suites (383 `@Test` in `studio/compile`, 60 files) and artifact-1 runner suites are deleted by name, counted per the 10.51 rule; v1 guided ITs are ported, not dropped; the benchmark harness becomes a repository artifact, not a scratchpad.

### What the code does today (design §1, condensed)

Guided input kinds are `nonsecretText | destination` and require a value. `GuidedSourceClassifier` already parses `<secret ID>` and requires it declared but emits configuration references only for `var`; the change is emission, not parsing. Every guided start fails `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED`. `knownSecrets` is always `[]`; the collector merges/withholds and wipes on dispose; sanitizer bound 64 × 4096. The collector **never exports a password control as a node** — hence the node-free target. The ordinary dispatch pass resolves secrets at dispatch only, erases on every exit path, carries `secretOrigins`; it has no password-only rule and no login detection. The observed replay job carries `accountHandle`; V33 DB functions require account fields; `AWAITING_AUTH` is in the V30 CHECK. `translation.enabled` is dead unless set (two gates). No production guided data exists; publication and observed replay default off; the guided worker has no `CMD`/chart (OBS-009).

# Security review record — secret-reference login in guided runs

Reviewer: Quinn (@qa, security-scan remit). Date: 2026-10-09. Subject: `secret-login-design.md` (Aria, 2026-10-09). Method: read-only verification of every load-bearing `path:line` claim against the working tree (116 uncommitted files treated as current); no code executed. "VERIFIED" = read in code; "INFERRED" = reasoned from code, not reproduced.

## Verdict

**PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS.** The design does not reopen the binding decision (no provider, no handoff, no cookie import; `installCookies` is deleted). Its dispatch-ordering, logging-sink and lifetime claims are accurate where they describe existing code. Two findings must be fixed in the design before stories are drafted (F-1, F-2); the rest become acceptance criteria.

Consequences: (a) the model cannot propose `fill.value=secretRef` on a `controlType:'password'` node because no such node exists; (b) §5's signature S cannot read `controlType==='password'` from `Observation.nodes`; (c) if the fix were to export password nodes, the `observation` pin and the sanitizer's threat model change. | Do **not** loosen the sanitizer for the model. The model emits `fill(secretRef)` with a target intent that names no node (new target kind, e.g. `{kind:'passwordControl', formId?}`); **trusted runner code** resolves the unique visible `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document at fill time (0 or >1 ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED`/clarification); the collector exports only a structural count (`coverage.passwordControls: n`, no name, no value) for §5 and for the validator's right-moment rule. | **F-2** | **HIGH (must fix wording; control is a condition)** | §4.6 I-A3 "no window" | Once released, a value is usable until the run ends. Legacy/replay children hold all declared secrets from `execute` until exit (≤ `STUDIO_TOTAL_RUNTIME`, default 120 s; run-deadline 600 s). Add `revoked` to `ExecutionControl` (and the guided `context`/`stop` path) so the dispatcher's revocation recheck cancels a live run before its next fill; audit a `REVOKED_MID_RUN` row. | `ExecutionControlService.java:31`; `application.yml:259`; `runCoordinator.ts:342-359` |
| F-3 | MEDIUM | §4 "Runner memory", I-C9 "scratch never receives values" | Browser profile is an unlisted disk sink. Legacy/replay use `launchPersistentContext` with the profile in scratch; guided uses `chromium.launch` with a temp user-data dir under `TMPDIR`. Chromium's password manager, autofill and form history write to `Login Data`/`Web Data`/`Preferences`; nothing disables them (grep for `password_manager|credentials_enable|Preferences`: none). Extend oracle C-3 to canary-scan the profile/scratch tree and the guided TMPDIR user-data dir **before** `runScratch.clear()`/browser close. State the residual (Chromium internals may still write transient files). | `browser.ts:90-110,466`; `scratchLayout.ts:4` |

Condition: parse the Vault read with a streaming `JsonParser` (`getTextCharacters`) and publish bodies as zeroable `byte[]` (`ofByteArray`), erased after send; `SecretValue` serializer writes via `JsonGenerator.writeString(char[],…)`. | `HashicorpStudioVaultProvider.java:350-360`; `HttpRunnerDispatchClient.java:113-116`; `GuidedRunnerClient.java:87-89` |

## Conditions for @sm (acceptance criteria to carry)

OBS-007
1. `secretRef` fill targets are resolved by trusted runner code to the unique visible `input[type=password]` in the top-level document at fill time; the model never receives a password node; ambiguity or absence is `POLICY_DENIED`; `observation` pin bumped for `coverage.passwordControls` (F-1).
2. `ExecutionControl` (and guided `stop`) carries `revoked`; a live run is cancelled within one control poll after revocation; audit row `REVOKED_MID_RUN`; I-A3 wording updated (F-2).
3. Profile `Preferences` disable password manager/autofill/session restore for both launch modes; canary scan of scratch/profile and TMPDIR user-data **before** clear/close returns zero hits (F-3).
4. Vault read via streaming parser to `char[]`; dispatch bodies published as `byte[]` and zeroed after send; `SecretValue.toString()`/`RunJob.toString()` print no value; residuals documented in evidence file (F-4).
5. One value bound (4096) enforced at create, bridge and sanitizer; `allowedOrigins` bounds unchanged (F-5).
6. `hasValue`/`inputValue` refused on `type=password` controls in legacy and observed executors; assertion messages never embed a password-control reading (F-6).
7. Runner replay digest excludes `secret`; test proves a byte-identical body differing only in `secret` yields the same digest (F-7).
8. `RunnerReport.secretUse` contract bump recorded in `openapi.yaml` and contract test (F-8).
9. All design §7 oracles implemented as listed, plus: Playwright raw-error capture variant of C-6; guided `capacity` assertion (F-10).

OBS-009 / OBS-010
10. Gates G-1, G-2 and new **G-3** (no scheduled secret-referencing run before production background and secret-use authorization sources exist) in release readiness and runbook (F-9).
11. Heap-dump/core-dump disabled in chart values with lint; Vault least-privilege policy test (design I-B7, I-C9).

No provider, handoff, account UI or cookie import is introduced; §4.5 deletes `installCookies`. F-1's trusted resolution keeps login author-owned via `<secret ID>`. Decision not reopened.

## 2. Target flow (one page)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports" / …
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight(mayUse + exists), no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS}  (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value = {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target = {kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}  (node-free: the collector never exports a password node)
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner proves exactly one visible enabled input[type=password] in the current top-level document
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal scope), RELEASE audit row, send BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → trusted runner re-resolves that unique password input at fill time (0 or >1 ⇒ POLICY_DENIED), origin ∈ allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins, withhold(value) BEFORE fill, fill via the pinned handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run by the ordinary dispatch pass, same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```

**4.1 Audit (SEC-9).** New append-only table `studio_secret_use_audit(id, occurred_at, path ∈ {GUIDED,OBSERVED_REPLAY}, execution_id?, session_id?, admission_id?, principal_id, csi_id, environment, test_id, secret_id, vault_version?, outcome ∈ {RESOLVED,NOT_AUTHORIZED,REVOKED,UNAVAILABLE,VAULT_UNAVAILABLE,REVOKED_MID_RUN})`, UPDATE/DELETE refused by trigger, written in the same transaction as the dispatch state change (replay: beside `recordDispatchPolicy`, `StudioDispatcher.java:322`). Never a value. Retention: existing retention pruner window unless Security asks otherwise (§8 Q3). T2 acceptance boundary: One immutable USAGE summary per declared secret under actual owner/attempt/declaration identity is required even for uncertain termination. Known USED may be committed early from verified PROGRESS; unknown and negative usage settle at terminal. Terminal reconciliation recognizes an already committed USED and never creates a second summary. Release/retry/live-recheck events do not create a second usage summary. Guided uses authentic ledger/admission evidence; replay uses authentic sparse `RunnerReport.secretUse`. Wire status remains exactly `USED|NOT_USED|REFUSED`: USED requires positive completed-use evidence, NOT_USED positive no-invocation/unreached evidence, REFUSED positive pre-effect refusal evidence. Missing child result, interrupted effect, mid-step kill or absent entry cannot synthesize NOT_USED or REFUSED. Resolved-but-proven-never-typed remains linked NOT_USED. Actual RELEASE and linked USAGE retain a nonnull resolution `outcome` from exactly `RESOLVED|NOT_AUTHORIZED|REVOKED|UNAVAILABLE|VAULT_UNAVAILABLE|REVOKED_MID_RUN`; RELEASE forbids usage_outcome and USAGE requires it. Audit-only uncertainty for released replay is one USAGE linked to its actual scoped RELEASE with `usage_outcome=UNKNOWN_OUTCOME`, or ACK_LOST only when acknowledgement loss is actually evidenced; neither is a wire status, a resolution outcome, a claimed usage fact or replay authority. Preserve positively committed usage facts. For observed replay, an authenticated PROGRESS report may carry only positively evidenced USED entries in the existing sparse secretUse map. Persist them only in the winning exact execution/accepted-history/attempt/admission/runnerInstance/sequence CAS transaction, after joining the frozen accepted artifact recipe and an actual completed secret-fill PASS receipt in the report. STARTED carries no usage facts; NOT_USED/REFUSED remain terminal-only. Arbitrary runner text, missing keys, failed/started steps, wrong recipes/attempts and payload reduction without supporting receipts cannot establish use. Later FINAL loss, cancel/reaper/unknown or sparse omission cannot overwrite already committed USED. No new wire field or status is introduced. Guided completion retains conservative OK→USED and every non-success→UNKNOWN_OUTCOME for each actual linked consumed secret admission; trusted backend no-send and authentic unreached facts retain their separately proven REFUSED/NOT_USED paths. A generic ledger ACK_LOST label alone never establishes actual acknowledgement loss. The present closed guided wire intentionally cannot transmit every private prewrite/post-fill fact; this does not authorize guessing. Prior committed positive facts remain immutable. No BridgeOutcome.secretUse field is added in this scope; any future completeness extension needs a separate explicit Aria proposal, fresh PO revalidation and root release. Three distinct no-decision variants are permitted: (1) true guided declared-but-unreached has one unlinked terminal USAGE/NOT_USED with null outcome/release_id/admission_id/vault_version/coordinate_ordinal and no fabricated release sequence. Its source_reference_id is the exact immutable configurationReferences.referenceId, coordinate_step_id is the declared source step, attempt is session:actual terminal owner fence, and full session/principal/CSI/environment/test/secret scope is authenticated against the immutable manifest and hash. A semantic obligation occurrence or selected-plan ordinal is never an actual action ordinal. Uniqueness is per actual declaration, independent of caller ordinal, sequence, timestamp or retention month. Distinct authentic source-reference declarations stay distinct. (2) guided committed consume with no committed resolution/release decision has one unlinked terminal uncertainty USAGE/UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (ACK_LOST only with separately authenticated actual acknowledgement-loss evidence), null outcome/release_id/vault_version and no fabricated release sequence, its actual nonnull admission_id/coordinate_step_id/coordinate_ordinal, dispatchCount1 and exact proposal→sourceInput→immutable reference/owner-fence binding. This variant may have had an ephemeral Vault read before crash: null means no committed decision, never zero reads or NOT_USED. (3) accepted OBSERVED_REPLAY declared-but-unattempted has one unlinked USAGE/NOT_USED only for an exact accepted execution/binding/revision/attempt/declared secret whose actual resolver path positively proves zero value-read entry for that ID and whose backend-owned atomic pre-send close or outage requeue proves transport was never entered. Outcome/release_id/vault_version/admission_id/guided coordinates are null; no release sequence is invented. The durable names-only no-send receipt and absence row commit with the owner transition. Missing decisionFacts, missing FINAL, post-send/no-admission ambiguity or a crash after possible read is insufficient. Other pre-send decisions, including genuine resolved-but-refused values, retain actual linked RELEASE/REFUSED facts. Retry authority stays separate: only existing genuine Vault-outage or definite transport refusal can authorize fresh attempt/grant/CAS; an absence receipt never grants retry. No admission/version/decision/release is fabricated and no extra Vault read or send is made for bookkeeping. Every other USAGE requires its actual scoped RELEASE. **4.2 Password-only fill (SEC-6) — ruling, restated after security review F-1.** The collector never exports a password control (§1), so the model cannot name one and the earlier "`controlType:'password'` at observation" rule was unimplementable. Rule: the model emits `fill(secretRef)` with the node-free target `{kind:"passwordControl", documentId, generation}`; **trusted runner code** resolves the target at `prepare` and again at the moment of the fill — exactly one visible, enabled `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document (frames excluded), pinned as an element handle, origin-checked (§4.3), filled through that handle so a type-flip after resolution fails on the handle. 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`; nothing typed. **Identity continuity (R1-1):** `generation` advances only per observation and `navigation` only on `framenavigated`, so a same-document DOM swap would otherwise let "re-resolve at fill" pick a different element. Resolution therefore runs **inside the collector's isolated world** under the existing `acquire`-style guard — cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call (`browser.ts:304-320`; `invoke` guard `:374`). The element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world; the fill requires that **the same element** is still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique visible candidate, and that `location.origin` read **in that world** (not `page.url()`) is in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill. **One function (R1-3):** "visible, enabled password input" is defined once in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots (`observationCollector.ts:134-137,259-260,418-431`) — and that same function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll` resolver is forbidden. Consequences stated: an off-screen but rendered decoy counts ⇒ ambiguous ⇒ refuse; frames and closed shadow roots are excluded ⇒ absent ⇒ refuse. **Form action (R1-2):** the fill is refused with `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` when the pinned input's owning `form.action` (resolved URL) has an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or when the input has no owning form and the document origin differs from the observed login document's origin. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts `passwordControl` only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; the proposal's `executionEvidence` still binds document/generation, so staleness checks are unchanged (I-A1 holds). **Limit (stated; accepted at GA — user default 2026-10-09, ADR-SC-005):** pages with two or more visible password fields (change-password, registration with confirm) are not supported for `secretRef` fills — the author gets `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing is typed, and there is no fallback adapter; a model-supplied ordinal/form narrowing is a reserved extension requiring its own Security review. Likewise a secret into a non-password control (TOTP, API token into a text field) is unsupported: the rule has **no opt-out** on the single path (§8 Q1, decided). Accepted because Vault is `none` in every value set today (GA plan C-3) and no shared environment has ever been deployed (panel 2026-10-09, devops), so no production secret-filling test exists.

**4.3 Origin binding (SEC-5).** Guided fill is permitted iff `executionEvidence.origin ∈ secret.allowedOrigins ∩ context.approvedOrigins`; the in-world resolution re-checks `location.origin` (§4.2, R1-1). Failure is `POLICY_DENIED` with nothing typed. **What an `allowedOrigins` entry asserts (R1-2):** the origin's **whole content is trusted** — the route allowlist is origin-granular (`browser.ts:119-123`) and the model, though it cannot `navigate` to arbitrary URLs (`runtime.ts:144-146`), can be steered by page text to **click** a same-origin link to attacker-authored content (user-generated content, stored XSS) presenting a single password field. Origin binding is therefore the trust boundary; the OBS-010 provisioning runbook must say so and secret owners must not list an origin that serves untrusted content. The `form.action` refusal (§4.2) is a cheap structural control on top. **Residual (stated):** same-origin script exfiltration of a typed value is not controllable by the runner. Replay performs the same check in the observed adapter (`secretOrigins` per ID; absent → bound to no origin); the `requireSecretOrigin` implementation in `playwrightAdapter.ts` is removed with the compile path and must not be what the test cites.

**4.4 Authorization scope (SEC-2).** Resolve through `VaultStudioReferenceResolver` with `VaultScope.of(scope.csiId, scope.environmentId, session.testId)` and `principal = scope.principalId` (the Run principal). `mayUse` at **start** (preflight, names only → `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` before any browser), at **prepare** (`GuidedDispatchService.prepareAndAdmit`, names only), and at **dispatch** (`resolve`, read + erase). Production `StudioSecretUseAuthorization` source remains GA item C-2 (not this wave). Cross-CSI: the KV path template includes `{csiId}/{environment}/{testId}` so a same-named secret under another CSI is `UnknownReference` → `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, never the other value.

**4.5 Cookie import (SEC-10).** Delete `observedAccountContext` (`browser.ts:181-193`), `RecordedContextCapability.installCookies/enter`, and the `context.addCookies` call. No gate, no flag: nothing in the decided flow needs it.

## 5. "Blocked by login" — detection and outcome code

**Code:** `LOGIN_REQUIRED` on both paths of the single generation — guided learn and observed replay. **Nature:** an *annotation of a failure that already happened*; it never turns a passing step into a failure or a failing step into a pass. **Detail:** `{stepId|stepIndex, loginStepsPresent}` so the UI can say either "This page asks you to sign in. Add login steps before step N using your secrets" (`false`) or "Your login steps did not sign you in; check the secret and the steps before step N" (`true`).

**Signature S(observation)**, trusted code only, no value reads, top-level document only (frames not inspected), one function for both paths: `observation.coverage.passwordControls ≥ 1` (the structural count the collector exports, §3 — password nodes themselves are never exported, `observationCollector.ts:395-396`) **and** ∃ exported visible+actionable node with `elementType ∈ {button, input}` or `role === 'button'`. The count is document-wide; no same-form correlation is available (R3: the legacy same-form probe is gone with `playwrightAdapter.ts`).

| Path | Where | Fire condition |
|---|---|---|
| Guided | Backend `GuidedTranslationService`, after the observation the current step's proposal attempt was grounded on; uses `coverage.passwordControls` (pin `observation: 3`) plus exported button nodes | The step's attempt ended in a validator rejection, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`/`MISSING_SOURCE`, or a `passwordControl` fill proposed without a `secretRef` input **and** S(current observation). `loginStepsPresent` = a `secretRef` fill was dispatched earlier in this session. Session → `FAILED`, result `failure.code=LOGIN_REQUIRED`. |
| Replay | `executor/observedReplay.ts` via the observed adapter, on the action that ends the run with `TARGET_DRIFT` or `POLICY_REFUSED` | The adapter already collected an observation for that action (`observedReplayAdapter.ts`); S(that observation) holds **and** the failing action is not itself a `secretRef` fill. `loginStepsPresent` = an earlier `secretRef` fill was performed in this run. Reported as the replay failure's annotation: `errorCode LOGIN_REQUIRED` with `detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}` added to `x-runner-error-codes`; the run stays `FAILED` and the drift step is still named for "Learn again" (incremental re-learn from that step, ADR-SC-005 D-D). |

**False-positive limits (stated).** Registration, change-password and card-CVV pages can match S; the hint then accompanies a run that was already failing, so the cost is a misleading sentence, bounded on guided by the fill-without-`secretRef` trigger and on replay by the drift/refusal trigger. S cannot correlate the button with the password field's form (the count is document-wide), so any page with an unrelated password widget plus any button matches once the step has already failed. Custom/obfuscated login forms without `type=password` are not detected (plain timeout). SSO pages on non-approved origins are blocked earlier by origin confinement and never reach S. Localized button text is deliberately **not** used.

**4.3 Origin binding (SEC-5).** Guided fill is permitted iff `executionEvidence.origin ∈ secret.allowedOrigins ∩ context.approvedOrigins`; the in-world resolution re-checks `location.origin` (§4.2, R1-1). Failure is `POLICY_DENIED` with nothing typed. **What an `allowedOrigins` entry asserts (R1-2):** the origin's **whole content is trusted** — the route allowlist is origin-granular (`browser.ts:119-123`) and the model, though it cannot `navigate` to arbitrary URLs (`runtime.ts:144-146`), can be steered by page text to **click** a same-origin link to attacker-authored content (user-generated content, stored XSS) presenting a single password field. Origin binding is therefore the trust boundary; the OBS-010 provisioning runbook must say so and secret owners must not list an origin that serves untrusted content. The `form.action` refusal (§4.2) is a cheap structural control on top. **Residual (stated):** same-origin script exfiltration of a typed value is not controllable by the runner. Replay performs the same check in the observed adapter (`secretOrigins` per ID; absent → bound to no origin); the `requireSecretOrigin` implementation in `playwrightAdapter.ts` is removed with the compile path and must not be what the test cites.

**4.4 Authorization scope (SEC-2).** Resolve through `VaultStudioReferenceResolver` with `VaultScope.of(scope.csiId, scope.environmentId, session.testId)` and `principal = scope.principalId` (the Run principal). `mayUse` at **start** (preflight, names only → `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` before any browser), at **prepare** (`GuidedDispatchService.prepareAndAdmit`, names only), and at **dispatch** (`resolve`, read + erase). Production `StudioSecretUseAuthorization` source remains GA item C-2 (not this wave). Cross-CSI: the KV path template includes `{csiId}/{environment}/{testId}` so a same-named secret under another CSI is `UnknownReference` → `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, never the other value.

**4.5 Cookie import (SEC-10).** Delete `observedAccountContext` (`browser.ts:181-193`), `RecordedContextCapability.installCookies/enter`, and the `context.addCookies` call. No gate, no flag: nothing in the decided flow needs it.

# Checks UI Studio — Architecture **Version:** 2.1 · **Date:** 2026-09-10 · **Status:** Design baseline; staging validation outstanding **Compiler amendment (2026-09-16):** [Studio inference contract v1](studio-inference-contract-v1.md) supersedes affected §§4/8 compiler decisions for the remediation stories: explicit unsupported outcomes, strict verdicts, atomic request/candidate identity, bounded inference, and versioned full/incremental authoring. Its [versioned OpenAPI](../specs/studio/inference.openapi.yaml) is declared, not yet deployed. Existing positional runner artifacts/routes remain unchanged. This document defines component ownership and technical contracts. [PRD §5.2](../../PRD.md#52-ui-testing-feature-checks-studio) and the [BRD](../brd/checks-ui-studio.brd.md) define product scope and GA criteria; [Epic 10](../epics/EPIC-10-EXECUTION.yaml) and its stories contain implementation order and acceptance tests. The [review](studio-execution-review.md) and [SSE assessment](studio-sse-viability.md) retain decision rationale. ## 1. Overview A support engineer writes an English checklist, reviews the proposed actions and Playwright source, confirms a revision, and runs it. Studio shows live step/log progress and private video evidence. Confirmed instructions remain immutable; application state and browser timing can still change outcomes. The editor, polling UI, video player and backend CRUD exist. Compilation, real execution, SSE and evidence storage remain to be built. Identity and vault code still contain temporary behavior; production-capable integrations are prerequisites for the credentialed pilot. ## 2. Scope | Capability | V1 | Later / excluded | |---|---|---| | Authoring | CSI-scoped English steps, variables/secret references, confirmed TypeScript artifact | No runtime AI or hand-written English translator; Python export retired | | Execution | On demand, Chromium, one page, initially one run per pod and 1–2 runner replicas | Scheduling, larger pools, other browsers, iframe/popup/multi-page workflows | | Progress | SSE current-state snapshots with GET recovery/fallback | Lossless event replay, WebSockets and live video | | Evidence | Native webm, private storage/download, attempted-step seek, 30-day expiry | Screenshots, transcoding and public video URLs | | Platform integration | Studio history and last-run summaries by CSI | Unified UI_TEST catalog/application-component/dashboard/report projections | Unsupported workflows must be explained before confirmation where detectable and fail explicitly otherwise. Pilot applications must support the approved single-page login flow; enterprise MFA is not assumed to work. ## 3. System architecture Each box below is a stack component; its subtitle states its core responsibility. Dashed arrows are authoring-time calls. Solid arrows carry user requests, execution, state or evidence.
